activities.anchor: But its settlement was the important part
activities.caption: pair each piece of 1688 with what it settled
activities.name: arContractMatch

config.prompt: 1688, the settlement — pair each piece with what it established:

pairs.right: the crown could not raise taxes, keep a standing army, or suspend laws without Parliament's consent
legitimate government rests on consent, protects life, liberty and property — and forfeits authority when it violates them
kings henceforth ruled through Parliament — established by coup, near-bloodless only in England
published from Holland, the logic radical enough to hide the author

config.why: The deeper precedent was intellectual: a regime could be justified by contract rather than by inheritance — the theory the next revolutions would pick up and radicalise.

activities.anchor: The American revolutionaries began as conservatives
activities.caption: bet before you read on — revolution from the start?
activities.name: arTaxPredict

config.q: 'No taxation without representation' — was it originally a revolutionary demand?
choices: Yes — the colonists set out from the first to found an independent nation
No — it began as a conservative demand to be treated as Britons; only when reconciliation failed did Jefferson restate the grievance in Locke's language
Yes — Locke drafted the Declaration before the fighting started
config.why: The revolutionaries began as conservatives claiming the traditional 'rights of Englishmen' — and ended with 'self-evident' truths, a written constitution with separated powers, and a contradiction over slavery that would cost a civil war.

activities.anchor: France's crisis was fiscal before it was philosophical
activities.caption: line up the summer of 1789, earliest first
activities.name: arSummerOrder

config.prompt: The nation replaces the crown — order these, earliest first:
items: the Estates-General meets for the first time in 175 years — May 1789
the Third Estate declares itself a National Assembly: sovereignty lives in the nation, not the crown
the Paris crowd storms the Bastille — July
the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen — August
config.why: The most condensed statement of the new order: 'Men are born and remain free and equal in rights.' Feudal privileges were abolished overnight and the Church's lands confiscated.

activities.anchor: the lesson every revolution since has had to absorb
activities.caption: find the faulty line — surviving your own success
activities.name: arTerrorSpot

config.prompt: One line of this French-revolution summary is wrong — click it:
lines: Wartime invasion, civil war in the Vendée and paranoid politics produced the Terror (1793–94).
The Committee of Public Safety executed some 17,000 people by guillotine — Danton among them.
Napoleon's Code Napoléon (1804) imposed equality before the law, careers open to talent and secular administration.
The man who crowned himself emperor did more than anyone to strengthen hereditary monarchy.
Peoples governed by foreigners could imagine themselves nations.
config.correction: Ironically, the emperor did more than anyone to kill hereditary monarchy as a self-evident institution.
config.why: 'Revolution devours its children' (Vergniaud, on the scaffold) became a pattern, not a quip — seizing power is easier than building what revolutionaries promised.

activities.anchor: The French colony of Saint-Domingue was the richest in the Americas
activities.caption: call the magnitude — the colony's engine
activities.name: arHaitiEstimate

config.prompt: At the 1791 revolt, roughly how many enslaved people worked Saint-Domingue's plantations?
config.why: About half a million, producing roughly half of Europe's sugar and coffee — the revolution they made defeated local militias, then Spanish, British and French armies, and founded the first Black republic in 1804.
config.context: Slaveholding powers refused recognition (the United States not until 1862); France extracted a crushing indemnity for the loss of 'property'.

activities.anchor: In one spring, revolutions broke out across around fifty European states
activities.caption: drag the divider — the barricades versus the agenda
activities.name: arAgendaCompare

config.prompt: 1848, defeat or agenda? Drag the divider:

before.label: the barricades — 1848–49
before.text: Almost every rising defeated within a year or two; the alliance of thrones held.

after.label: the agenda — a generation later
after.text: Italy (1861, completed 1870) and Germany (1871) unified as nation-states, France a republic again, serfdom and absolutism permanently on the defensive.

config.why: The Springtime of Peoples failed and, in failing, taught its ideas to the organisers of everything that followed — revolutions are judged on the survival of their agenda, not on the fate of the barricades.

activities.anchor: Not every transformation needed to overthrow a king
activities.caption: line up Japan's borrowed modernity, earliest first
activities.name: arMeijiOrder

config.prompt: Japan without a revolution in the streets — order these, earliest first:
items: American warships force Japan's ports open — 1853–54
reformers 'restore' the emperor as a symbol while dismantling feudal rule — 1868
the Iwakura mission travels abroad to copy constitutions, industry and universities — 1871–73
Japan defeats Russia — the first non-European state to beat a European great power — 1905
config.why: Within a generation Japan executed one of history's fastest modernisations on purpose — state-built railways and mines, conscription, compulsory schooling — shattering the assumption that the revolutionary-industrial package was a Western monopoly.
